did_you_know.text: Did you know? David identified the place where the house of the Lord would be built and declared that it was also the place for Israel’s burnt-offering altar.
Did you know? David gathered the resident foreigners in the land of Israel and appointed stonecutters to prepare dressed stones for building the house of God.
Did you know? David prepared large quantities of iron for the nails, the doors of the gates, and the fittings, as well as an unweighable amount of bronze.
Did you know? The cedar logs prepared for the building came to David from the Sidonians and the Tyrians, who brought them in abundance.

Did you know? David explained that he was preparing the building materials in advance because Solomon was still young and inexperienced, and the house of the Lord was to be great, magnificent, and renowned throughout all the lands.
Did you know? According to the word of the Lord, David would not build the house because he had shed much blood and fought great wars; the task of building the house was assigned to Solomon.
Did you know? Solomon is described as a “man of rest” because the Lord promised to give him rest from all his enemies and to grant Israel peace and quiet during his reign.
Did you know? Solomon was the one appointed to build the house for the name of the Lord, and the verse describes his special relationship with the Lord: “He will be my son, and I will be his father.”
Did you know? David taught Solomon that the success of his leadership depended on wisdom, understanding, and keeping the law of the Lord—not merely on his ability to build the house.

Did you know? David said that he had prepared for the house of the Lord one hundred thousand talents of gold and one million talents of silver, along with large quantities of bronze, iron, wood, and stone; he added that Solomon should add to them.
Did you know? In addition to the building materials, many skilled workers were available to Solomon: stonecutters, craftsmen in stone and wood, and every skilled worker in every kind of craft.

Did you know? David called on Israel’s leaders to devote their hearts and souls to seeking the Lord and building the sanctuary, so that they could bring into it the Ark of the Covenant of the Lord and the holy vessels.
